pr.title: feat(scm): detect worktree hierarchy from inside and outside primary worktree closes #259083 #267612 #259083
pr.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->
## Prerequisites
This PR improves recently introduced git worktree support.
1. Worktree detection improvements.
Worktree hierarchy in the `repository` tab of the SCM view is shown only when the **primary worktree** is open  as described in #259083 and upstream issues.
2. `${activeRepositoryName}` `window.title` variable
Currently, it simply shows the folder name of the _open worktree_.
By showing the `primary` worktree folder name instead, we'll support other variations to customize window.title.
If someone wants to stick to open worktree folder name, they can simply use `${folderName}` variable.
The detailed use-case is described in #251596.

The reason I combined these changes in a single PR is that primary repository name derivation is tightly coupled with the way SCM detects worktrees.

## Setup
```bash
mkdir test-folder && cd test-folder
git init repo && cd repo
touch test.txt && git add . && git commit -m "init" # introduce first commit
git worktree add test-worktree-inside
git worktree add ../test-worktree-outside
```
### Scenario 1: Opening the primary worktree 
It shouldn't be any different. Hierarchy is shown within the SCM view + worktrees are detected.
### Scenario 2: Opening the `test-worktree-inside` worktree
Should have the same output as Scenario 1.
### Scenario 3: Opening the `test-worktree-outside`
Should have the same output as Scenario 1.

## Notes
I could decouple the changes and submit another PR if required.
Also, I don't see any unit tests for the SCM `model.ts`. Let me know if I should add test coverage.
Although this PR improves worktree detection, it still doesn't support hierarchy using worktrees with bare repositories as reported in #267606

reviews.body:
## Pull Request Overview

This PR enhances Git worktree handling in SCM by (1) ensuring the primary worktree is opened first to enable consistent worktree hierarchy discovery and (2) updating active repository context (e.g. for window title variable) to prefer the primary worktree name. It also introduces metadata (primaryWorktreePath) to link secondary worktrees back to their primary repository.
- Automatically redirects opening a standalone worktree to first open its primary.
- Adjusts active repository context resolution to use parent (primary) repository when applicable.
- Extends IDotGit with primaryWorktreePath to support hierarchy awareness.

### Reviewed Changes

Copilot reviewed 3 out of 3 changed files in this pull request and generated 2 comments.

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| src/vs/workbench/contrib/scm/browser/activity.ts | Uses parent repository name for active repository context when in a worktree. |
| extensions/git/src/model.ts | Adds early-return logic to open primary worktree before a secondary and skips opening the secondary directly. |
| extensions/git/src/git.ts | Extends git metadata with primaryWorktreePath for worktree relationship resolution. |

comments.body: @lszomoru sorry for pinging you, looks like this PR and related issues fell through the cracks, could you take a look?

This PR seems awesome! It covers all my current issues that I feel made worktrees not feel well supported in VSCode.

- Opening a worktree does not show the "parent" Git project any longer in Repositories view
- The VSCode title changes from displaying the project name to the branch name

So I'm all in favor of this update to `${activeRepositoryName}`! @lszomoru any change to get this PR rolling again?
@csvn Happy to push this forward if @lszomoru agrees on the approach

Just coming from far left field, but having this change land, would directly support the new `--worktree` feature we are just adding to our `docker sandbox` command, so totally in favor to move this forward 👍

Will this also work with worktrees coming off bare repos?  My current organization structure is:

{repo_name}/.bare.git
{repo_name}/main  -- worktree of main branch
{repo_name}/feat1 -- worktree of feature 1
{repo_name}/release/0.1 -- worktree of release/0.1 branch
